# Evidence
- Problem class: go-ledger-compaction-sparse-agg-seqs-verify-false-holes
- Model: openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash
- Solved: 2026-10-22T20:41:49.836Z
- Verification: solution produced by pi in sandbox; see signatures.json

signatures.description:
SYMPTOM: a single successful `ledger compact` made the product's own `ledger verify`
report the compacted generation as corrupt. Measured on a live day: exit 0 from compact
(delta -99126 bytes, 103 aggregates), then verify returned FINDINGS exit 1 with
seq_holes=25 (holes exactly where compaction had aggregated event lines: 88..99,
650..658, ...) and tombstone_mismatches=101. An operator following the documented
integrity ladder would read healthy compacted data as data loss.

ROOT CAUSE (two halves, both needed):

1. The aggregate payload declared its consumed seqs as a CONTIGUOUS SPAN
   `agg_seqs = {first, last, count, exceptions}`. But compaction folds one group's
   event lines while groups INTERLEAVE in the writer, so one group's folded seqs are
   sparse — measured fixture: group A folds seqs 2,5,8,11 (first=2,last=11), group B
   folds 3,6,9,12, group C folds 4,7,10,13. The span [2..11] therefore both omitted the
   consumed seqs of its own group's later folds and OVERLAPPED other groups' ranges, so
   no verifier could reconstruct consumption from it. Fix: record the explicit,
   deduplicated, ascending consumed seq list (`agg_seqs.seqs`) and keep first/last/count/
   exceptions for compatibility; when re-compacting a prior aggregate, carry its own seq
   list forward.

2. Neither verifier read `agg_seqs` at all. The seq walk required rec.Seq == prev+1, and
   the tombstone reconciliation counted only surviving event lines. Fix: one shared reader
   (`aggSeqSpans`: prefer the explicit list, fall back to [first..last] minus exceptions
   for older aggregates), one continuity function (a seq is accounted for by a LINE or by
   an aggregate's declared range), and one tombstone denominator (declared ranges + only
   those surviving event lines whose own seq falls INSIDE a declared range — a line the
   aggregate did not fold must not inflate the count).

SECOND DEFECT FOUND BY CI: the first cut accumulated every walked day into one seq set, so
a multi-day walk (verify with no --day) became blind to a real per-day hole whenever another
day carried that seq, and the old global `prev` walk invented a hole at every day boundary.
Fix: seq continuity is PER-DAY — flush accumulated seqs/consumed ranges at each day boundary.

VERIFICATION: new compact-then-verify round trip (compact a day with events+folds+spine,
then both the library verifier and the read-only CLI verifier must return OK with zero holes
and zero tombstone mismatches) plus a negative half (drop one aggregate line and verify must
still FAIL, so the accounting does not blind the gate). Existing corruption tests
(MidFileCorruptLine, InteriorCorruption, live-fold false positive) stay green.

GENERAL RULE: when a compaction/reduction step replaces N records with one summary record,
the summary must state the EXACT set/range it consumed (not a bounding range) and every
consumer that validates completeness must consult it; interleaved sources make bounding
ranges overlap and lie. Validate the reduction round-trip in a test, and make continuity
checks per-partition (per day/segment) rather than across the whole walk.
signatures.environment: Go 1.26, Linux; append-only JSONL ledger with generation files; groups interleaved in a single writer
